findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, not lazily
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an immediately invoked import() (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` on line 3 and likewise for all ~29 apps). Evaluating this object when the module is first imported therefore starts loading every app at once, so importing appStore from any file (getCalendar, videoClient, payment handlers, routers) still pulls in all apps and defeats the lazy/on-demand loading this PR is meant to achieve. The values need to be thunks (e.g. `() => import(...)`) with call sites invoking them, or an equivalent lazy lookup, to actually defer loading until an app is requested.

findings.title: appStore value type changed from module to Promise without a compatible accessor
findings.body: appStore previously mapped each key to a module namespace object, so consumers could synchronously use `appStore[key].lib`, `'lib' in appStore[key]`, etc. It now maps each key to a Promise of the module, which is not backward compatible: any consumer not converted to `await appStore[key]` in this PR will receive a Promise, find no `lib` property (`'lib' in promise` is false), and silently skip calendar/video/payment functionality (or fail type-checking). This PR only updates a subset of call sites, so the exported contract break needs either a full audit/conversion of every appStore consumer or a compatibility-preserving accessor.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, the actual `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls no longer even start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and on serverless/request completion the deletions may never run, leaving stale calendar/video events. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) also cannot catch rejections from the async callback, so failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a for...of loop) so deletion completes and errors are handled.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` no longer start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and if the request/process ends first the deletions are lost, leaving stale calendar/video events. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback, so failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a for...of loop).

findings.title: async forEach callback makes reschedule deletion fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards each callback's promise. The mutation then immediately sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns, so the calendar/video deletions for the old booking may not have started, let alone finished; if the request context is torn down they are silently dropped and the old events remain. Rejections inside the callback are also unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` before sending email/webhooks.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials...forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` runs its pushes only after awaiting getCalendar (now a dynamic import) and deleteEvent. Later, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) snapshots whatever apiDeletes contains at that moment, so entries pushed afterwards are never awaited; the handler can delete booking references/attendees and report success while the recurring calendar events are never deleted. Convert this branch to a for...of loop or collect the per-credential work with Promise.all and push/await those promises, as was done for the non-recurring branch.
